column1: # Example ARTEFACTS the MII KDS module template ships and step 3 DELETES.
# ONE definition, read by two programs. `verify-migration.py` check R4 uses these
# tokens to find links into template scaffolding that no longer exists;
# `autofix-fix.py` class `template-example-link` uses the SAME tokens to remove
# those links. They were previously a bare inline literal (`example-patient`)
# duplicated in both files, so a template that renamed its example would have
# left the check and the fixer silently disagreeing about what a template example
# is -- the fixer stripping links the check no longer raises, or the check
# raising findings the fixer cannot see.
# WHY A LINK TO ONE OF THESE IS SAFE TO REMOVE MECHANICALLY: the module's own
# narrative predates the template, so it cannot have referenced the template's
# examples. A link that names one can only have come from the template's
# scaffolding, which step 3 deletes. That provenance argument -- not the string
# itself -- is what makes the class auto-fixable, and it holds only for artefacts
# the TEMPLATE owns. Anything a module ships is out of scope here.
# Columns:
#   token             substring identifying a link target as a template example.
#   template_version  the ig-template PACKAGE version this was verified against
#                     (`ig-template/package/package.json` .version), NOT the
#                     module-template REPO tag -- repo v0.6.0 vendors package
#                     0.5.1, and confusing the two produces a confident, wrong
#                     finding (spec 11.4).
#   verified_on       the date the token was measured in that template.
#   why               what it names.
# WHEN THE TEMPLATE CHANGES: re-measure against the vendored package and add or
# replace a row here. Nothing else needs editing.
# template_tag: v0.11.1
token
example-patient
column4: the template's example Patient profile + instance and their pages, deleted by step 3 (re-verified at module-template v0.11.1, which vendors ig-template package 1.3.2: input/fsh/profiles/example-patient.fsh + instances/example-patient-instance.fsh)
